p_question-6361.ja:
以下は、留学生の作文である。


農業ボランティア

ゴメス　フランシスコ

　半年前、私は友達に誘われて、働き手が足りない農家を手伝う「農業ボランティア」を始めた。過去にごみ拾いなどのボランティアはしたことがあったが、農業ボランティアのことは友達に聞くまで知らなかった。私は日本でいろいろな経験をしたいと思っていたので、参加することにした。

　私が手伝っているのは南さんという農家だ。40代のご夫婦がトマトやキャベツなど、いろいろな野菜を作っている。農作業は初めての経験だったが、農業は想像していた以上に知識や経験が必要だと感じた。[48]、収穫のタイミングは、成長の具合や天気予報を基に、いつがいいかを判断しなければならない。また、トマトなどは成長の段階に応じて与える水の量を変えないとしっかり育たない。体力[49]必要で、農業は本当に大変な仕事だ。

　初めのころは、わからないことが多く、よく質問をして南さんたちの作業を止めてしまっていた。手伝いではなく邪魔をしているのではないかと不安になることもあった。それでも、「ありがとう。助かっているよ。」といつも声をかけてくれたので、だんだん自分も役に立てていると感じられるようになった。収穫したばかりのトマトを初めて食べさせてもらったときはあまりにおいしくて[50]。収穫したときの達成感や大切に育てた野菜を味わう喜びは、このボランティアに参加しなければ感じられなかっただろう。

　農業ボランティアとして役に立てたことがうれしかったし、多くの貴重な経験をすることができた。[51]本当によかったと思う。

The following is an essay by an international student.


Farm Volunteering

Gomez Francisco

Six months ago, at a friend’s invitation, I started “farm volunteering,” helping farms that lack enough workers. I had done volunteer activities like trash pickup before, but I didn’t know about farm volunteering until my friend told me. Since I wanted to have a variety of experiences in Japan, I decided to take part.

The farm I help at is run by the Minami family. A couple in their forties grows various vegetables such as tomatoes and cabbages. It was my first experience doing farm work, and I felt that farming requires more knowledge and experience than I had imagined. [48] For example, you have to judge the right time to harvest based on growth conditions and the weather forecast. Also, with tomatoes and the like, if you don’t change the amount of water according to the growth stage, they won’t grow properly. Physical stamina is [49] necessary, and farming is truly a demanding job.

At first there were many things I didn’t understand, and I often stopped the Minamis’ work with my questions. I sometimes worried that I was getting in the way rather than helping. Even so, they always said, “Thank you—you’re a big help,” so I gradually came to feel that I was being useful too. The first time they let me eat a just-harvested tomato, it was so delicious [50]. The sense of accomplishment at harvest and the joy of savoring vegetables carefully grown are feelings I probably wouldn’t have had if I hadn’t joined this volunteer activity.

I was happy that I could be useful as a farm volunteer, and I was able to gain many valuable experiences. [51] I truly think it was great.

p_question-6370.ja:
（１）

　新年度が始まった。進級や進学、転勤やそれに伴う転居など変化の多い季節だ。新しい学校に進学したり職場を変わったりして新しい環境に入っていく人も多いだろう。（中略）

　新しい環境では緊張や不安を感じるものだ。人見知り（注1）が強い性格だと、こうした変化が苦手だ。私もその一人だが、どんな場所でもいつも通り元気に自分の力を発揮する人を見ると、うらやましくも思える。こちらは少々なことで気持ちが揺れ動いているように思え、いつでも平常心で行動できればと考える。

　しかし新しい環境で不安を感じないというのは、必ずしも良いことではない。慣れない環境で、何の不安も感じずにこれまでと同じような行動をしていたのでは、思いがけない失敗をする可能性がある。これまでの経験からは想定（注2）できないことが起きるかもしれない。人生、何があるかわからないのだ。

　慣れない場所では、むしろ良くないことが起きる可能性を考えて慎重に行動した方が安全だ。私たちは不安を感じるからこそ、良くない事態に備えて準備しようと考える。緊張するからこそ、集中して、しかも慎重に問題に対応できる。実際に良くないことが起きたときの対応法もシミュレーション（注3）できる。

　不安や緊張は自分を守る安全弁（注4）の働きをしている。不安や緊張を感じたときは、そのような気持ちを感じられる自分のこころの力を信じて、あれこれ考えすぎずに今日自分にできることに集中するようにしてほしい。

（注1）人見知り：初対面の相手に緊張する気持ち（注2）想定する：ここでは、想像する（注3）シミュレーションする：ここでは、想像する（注4）安全弁：ここでは、安全のための装置

(1)

　A new academic and fiscal year has begun. It is a season of many changes: moving up a grade, advancing to a new school, job transfers, and relocations that accompany them. Many people will be entering new environments by starting at a new school or changing workplaces. (Omitted)

　In a new environment, it is natural to feel tension and anxiety. For those with a strongly shy disposition (Note 1), such changes are difficult. I am one of them, and when I see people who can be as lively as ever and display their abilities anywhere, I feel a bit envious. I feel that my own emotions sway at the slightest thing, and I wish I could always act with a calm mind.

　However, not feeling anxious in a new environment is not necessarily a good thing. If you act in the same way as before in an unfamiliar setting without feeling any anxiety, you may make unexpected mistakes. Things that cannot be anticipated (Note 2) from your past experience may occur. In life, you never know what will happen.

　In unfamiliar places, it is actually safer to consider that something unfavorable might happen and to act cautiously. Precisely because we feel anxious, we think to prepare for adverse situations. Precisely because we feel tension, we can concentrate and deal with problems carefully. We can even simulate (Note 3) how to respond if something bad actually occurs.

　Anxiety and tension function as a safety valve (Note 4) that protects us. When you feel anxiety or tension, trust in the strength of your mind that allows you to feel such emotions, and without overthinking, try to focus on what you can do today.

(Note 1) Shyness: the feeling of being tense with people you meet for the first time(Note 2) to anticipate: here, to imagine(Note 3) to simulate: here, to imagine(Note 4) safety valve: here, a device for safety

p_question-6372.ja:
（２）　

「いぬ」は人間の家畜（注１）になる前から、群れで暮していた動物です。人間の家族の一員ともなれば集団生活の掟（注２）のままに、飼い主を群れのリーダーや上位のものとみなし（注３）、日頃から服従の態度（注４）を示します。また、飼い主のその日の顔色を窺うなど、家庭内の空気を読みとりながら、上手にふるまう（注５）ことにも長け（注６）ています。群れで生活する動物は、お互いの状況を把握して（注７）、それにあわせた行動をとることが、群れ社会のなかで生きていくには必要だからです。人間にとっても、「いぬのきもち」は非常にわかりやすく、会話はできなくとも、お互いになにを考えているかが理解しやすい動物です。そこが、「いぬ」と一緒に暮すことのひとつの魅力でもあるのでしょう。

　一方、「ねこ」は、もともとが単独で行動していた動物ですので、家の中で人間の家族と一緒に暮すようになっても、協調性のようなものはありません。また、家族の中での自分の立場もあまり気にしないので、いぬのように、飼い主をリーダーとみなして服従することはありません。（中略）ねこがいったい飼い主である自分のことをどう思っているのか、飼い主であれば誰しも知りたいところですが、人間の持つ気持ちや感情の尺度では、完全には理解しがたい動物だと思います。ねこはそもそも集団生活をしない、個を重視する孤独な生き物だからです。しかし、この理解できないところが、ねこの大きな魅力のひとつであり、人間が、ねこと一緒に暮したがる理由のひとつではないでしょうか。

(注1) 家畜：人間が飼って利用する動物

(注2) 掟：ここでは、決まり

(注3) みなす：考える

(注4) 服従の態度：ここでは、従う態度

(注5) ふるまう：行動する

(注6) 長ける：優れている

(注7) 把握する：ここでは、理解する

(2)　

Dogs are animals that lived in packs even before they became human livestock (Note 1). Once they become members of a human family, they follow the rules (Note 2) of group living, regard (Note 3) their owner as the pack leader or a superior member, and routinely show a submissive attitude (Note 4). They are also adept (Note 6) at behaving skillfully (Note 5) by reading the atmosphere at home, such as by watching their owner’s expression that day. For animals that live in groups, grasping (Note 7) each other’s situations and taking actions accordingly is necessary for survival within pack society. For humans, too, a dog’s feelings are very easy to understand; even though we cannot converse, it is easy to grasp what each of us is thinking. That is likely one of the charms of living together with dogs.

By contrast, cats originally acted alone, so even when they come to live with a human family, they have little in the way of cooperativeness. They also do not care much about their position within the family, so unlike dogs, they do not regard the owner as leader and submit. (Omitted) Every cat owner wants to know what their cat thinks of them, but I believe cats are animals that cannot be fully understood using human scales of feelings and emotions. Cats are solitary creatures that value the individual and do not live in groups to begin with. However, this very inscrutability is one of cats’ great charms and one of the reasons people want to live with them.

(Note 1) livestock: animals kept and used by humans

(Note 2) rules: here, norms or codes

(Note 3) regard: to consider

(Note 4) submissive attitude: here, an attitude of obedience

(Note 5) behave: to act

(Note 6) adept: excellent

(Note 7) grasp: here, to understand

p_question-6374.ja:
（３）

　作家が小説を書くときは、頭の中に書いているシーンが「絵」や「映像」として浮かんでいます。そのシーンを言語化し、文字という記号にしているのです。読者は作家が書いた文字を読み、頭の中で想像しながら映像化します。そこで感情移入（注１）が起きて、笑ったり、涙したりしているのです。

　小説がベストセラー（注２）となり映画化されると「この配役じゃない」（注３）「そのシーンは違う」といった声がよく上がりますが、これは当たり前のことです。映画というのは監督が原作を読んでイメージを膨らませ、映像化した作品だからです。原作の小説は読者一人一人が作家からの記号（文字）を受け取って、それぞれが自由にシーンを思い浮かべています。

　フランスの哲学者ロラン・バルトはこの現象を「作者の死」と表現しました。

「物語は作者の意図通りに読まなくてもいい。読者が好きな読み方をして、それぞれ解釈すればいい」

「作者は作品を支配できず、読者に解釈を任せなければならない」

ロラン・バルトはそう主張しました。私たちは作品の解釈を作者に求めがちです。これは作者の意図を正確に読み取ろうという発想です。そうではなく、作品の解釈は読者それぞれでいい。読者それぞれが頭の中で好き勝手に映像化していいのです。

(注１) 感情移入：ここでは、登場人物と同じ気持ちになること(注２) ベストセラー：最もよく売れている本(注３) この配役じゃない：ここでは、演じている俳優がこの役に合っていない

(3)

　When a novelist writes, the scenes they are writing appear in their mind as “pictures” or “images.” They put those scenes into language, turning them into the symbols we call letters. Readers then read those letters, imagine, and turn them back into images in their minds. That is where empathy (Note 1) occurs, leading us to laugh or to shed tears.

　When a novel becomes a bestseller (Note 2) and is adapted into a film, people often say, “This casting is wrong” (Note 3) or “That scene is different,” but this is only natural. A film is a work in which the director reads the original, expands their own images, and visualizes them. With the original novel, each reader receives the author’s symbols (letters) and freely pictures the scenes in their own way.

　The French philosopher Roland Barthes described this phenomenon as “the death of the author.”

“A story need not be read strictly according to the author’s intention. Readers may read as they like and each interpret it.”

“The author cannot control the work; interpretation must be left to the reader.”

So argued Roland Barthes. We tend to ask the author for the interpretation of a work—an approach that seeks to read the author’s intent precisely. Instead, interpretation can be left to each reader. Each reader is free to visualize it in their own mind as they wish.

(Note 1) empathy: here, to feel the same as the characters (Note 2) bestseller: a book that sells the most (Note 3) “This casting is wrong”: here, the actor playing the role does not fit it

p_question-6376.ja:
（４）

　哲学は一般の人が、一般的な問題について考えるための学問です。「人生の意味とは何か」「人類に共通の利益はあるのか」「時間とは何か」「愛とは何か」「正義 (注1) はどのように定まるのか」「国家はどのようにあるべきか」「法の役割とは何か」「正しい認識 (注2) にはどうやって到達するのか」「宗教は必要か」などが哲学の典型的な問いです。

　これらの問いは、複数の教科や学問分野の根底 (注3) に関わるような問題であることはおわかりでしょう。「愛とは何か」を考えることは、個人的な愛についての考えを尋ねているだけではなく、隣人愛 (注4) は、社会のなかで人々のつながりはどうあるべきか、家族愛は、家族とはどうあるべきかといった、社会におけるみんなの問題となってくるはずです。社会観や家族観は、政策 (注5) や法律の設定とも関係してくるでしょう。（中略）

　しかし哲学のもうひとつの重要な仕事は、それぞれの専門的な知識を、より一般的で全体的な観点から問い直すことです。たとえば、遺伝子治療 (注6) は非常に専門性が高い分野です。しかし遺伝子治療の範囲をどこまで認めていいのか。遺伝子を組み替えて難病にかかりにくくした子どもを作っていいのか。人間の遺伝子に対して、人間はどこまで改変 (注7) してよいものなのでしょうか。

　こうしたことは、社会のだれにでも関わってくるので、医学の専門家だけに判断を任せてよい問題ではありません。社会に存在している常識や知識や技術を、人間の根本的な価値に照らし合わせてあらためて検討することは重要な哲学の役割です。

(注1) 正義：人としての正しい行い

(注2) 認識：ここでは、理解

(注3) 根底：土台

(注4) 隣人愛：ここでは、社会で交流のある人への愛

(注5) 政策：政治の方針と手段

(注6) 遺伝子治療：遺伝子に働きかける治療法

(注7) 改変する：変える

(4)

　Philosophy is a discipline for ordinary people to think about ordinary—universal—problems. Typical philosophical questions include: “What is the meaning of life?”, “Is there a common good for humankind?”, “What is time?”, “What is love?”, “How is justice (Note 1) determined?”, “How ought the state to be?”, “What is the role of law?”, “How do we reach correct understanding (Note 2)?”, and “Is religion necessary?”

　You can see that these questions relate to issues at the foundation (Note 3) of multiple subjects and academic fields. Considering “What is love?” is not merely asking about personal love; questions such as neighborly love (Note 4)—how people’s bonds should be in society—and familial love—how the family ought to be—become issues for everyone in society. Views of society and of the family will also be connected to the setting of policy (Note 5) and laws. (Omitted)

　Another important task of philosophy is to reexamine specialized bodies of knowledge from a more general and holistic perspective. For example, gene therapy (Note 6) is a highly specialized field. But to what extent should we permit gene therapy? Is it acceptable to recombine genes to create children less likely to develop serious diseases? How far may humans ethically modify (Note 7) the human genome?

　Such matters concern everyone in society, so they should not be left solely to medical experts to decide. It is an important role of philosophy to reconsider the common sense, knowledge, and technologies that exist in society in light of fundamental human values.

A


　Many people feel they are not good at memorizing. While it’s understandable to feel frustrated when cramming doesn’t stick, it’s a problem to assume you can’t remember because your memory is inherently poor. People who are good at memorization are not born with better memories; they devise better ways to memorize.

　When memorizing, it is effective not only to look with your eyes but also to engage other senses. By reading aloud, you input information through your ears as well, making it more secure. By writing, you organize vague content and can understand it more logically. In this way, by stimulating the brain through several senses, you can boost your memory.

多くのマネジャーやリーダーの人たちに聞くと、部下や後輩に対しては、「なんでも相談するのではなく、自分で工夫して取り組んでほしい」「次にやるべきことを自分で考えて、動いてほしい」という思いをもっています。

　ところが一方で、同じマネジャーやリーダーの人から、「自分がやったほうが早い」「育てている暇がない」といった言葉も洩れてきます。部下や後輩に育ってほしいと願ってはいるものの、そのために自分の時間を割いて教え育てる時間の余裕も心の余裕もないというところなのでしょう。

　確かに部下や後輩を育成するのはとてもやっかいで時間がかかります。新入社員を育てる場合には、仕事を細かく一つひとつを教え込んで理解させ、させてみて、フィードバック（注1）することを繰り返す必要があり、相当のエネルギーを費や（注2）さなければなりません。中堅社員（注3）や中途採用者であれば、一人ひとりの個性や能力を考慮しながら対応しなければならないというむずかしさがあります。基本的な職務遂行力（注4）があり、経験もプライドもある人に何をどこまで教えればよいのか。丁寧に教えすぎれば、「そのくらいはわかっています」と反発されるかもしれないし、大丈夫だろうと放置（注5）していたら、実は何もわかっていなかったということにもなりかねません。メンバーの主体的な努力をうまく引き出しながら、方向づけをして、しかもよい結果や成果が得られるよう支援していく手加減（注6）が大変むずかしいのです。

（中略） 

　育てようとすることで、みえてくるものがたくさんあります。たとえば、自分にとってとても簡単なことでも、相手になかなか理解してもらえないことがあると気づきます。物事を理解するにもスタイルがあって、個人によってそれは異なるのだとわかります。したがってこの方法がだめならば、今度はこちらの方法で説明しようと、教えるためにはさまざまな工夫が求められます。口頭で説明したけれど理解されなかったので、今度は、紙に絵を描きながら説明しようというように、いろいろな角度からいろいろな方法を使い分けていくことも学びます。

　教えることを通じて、自分でもよく理解していなかったと気づくこともあります。教えるためには曖昧なところ、理解の不十分なところがないように勉強しなければなりません。勉強することで、自分の知識やスキル（注7）がまた上がるのです。

(注1) フィードバックする：ここでは、成果に対してコメントを返す

(注2) 費やす：使う

(注3) 中堅社員：主力となって働いている社員

(注4) 職務遂行力：仕事をやり抜く能力

(注5) 放置する：放っておく

(注6) 手加減：ここでは、調整のしかた

(注7) スキル：技術

When we ask many managers and leaders, they say of their subordinates and juniors, “I don’t want them to come to me about everything; I want them to use their own ingenuity and tackle things,” and “I want them to think for themselves about what to do next and take action.”

　On the other hand, the very same managers and leaders also let slip remarks such as, “It’s faster if I do it myself,” and “I don’t have time to train them.” They want their subordinates and juniors to grow, but they likely lack both the time to spare and the mental leeway to devote themselves to teaching and developing them.

　Indeed, developing subordinates and juniors is troublesome and time-consuming. When training new employees, you must teach the job step by step in detail, ensure they understand it, have them try it, and repeatedly provide feedback (Note 1), which requires considerable energy (Note 2). For mid-career employees (Note 3) and mid-career hires, there is the added difficulty of responding while considering each person’s individuality and ability. How much, and what, should you teach to those who already have the basic ability to perform their duties (Note 4), experience, and pride? If you teach too carefully, they may push back, saying, “I already know that much,” but if you assume they’re fine and leave them alone (Note 5), it may turn out they understood nothing. It is extremely difficult to strike the right balance (Note 6): to draw out members’ independent efforts, provide direction, and at the same time support them so that good results and outcomes are achieved.

(Omitted) 

　By attempting to develop others, many things come into view. For example, you realize that even things that are very easy for you may be hard for others to understand. You learn that people have different styles of understanding and that these differ from person to person. Therefore, if one method fails, you must devise another to teach—explaining this time in a different way. If a verbal explanation didn’t work, next time you might draw pictures on paper as you explain. You learn to use different methods from different angles.

　Through teaching, you may also discover that you yourself did not fully understand something. To teach, you must study so that there are no ambiguities or areas of insufficient understanding. By studying, your own knowledge and skills (Note 7) improve again.

(Note 1) to give feedback: here, to return comments on results

(Note 2) to expend: to use

(Note 3) mid-career employees: core members who serve as a main workforce

(Note 4) ability to perform duties: the capability to carry work through

(Note 5) to leave alone: to neglect

(Note 6) right balance: here, the way of adjusting

(Note 7) skills: techniques

Answer 2: 完了 is correct. It means "completion" or "completion of a task."

**Question Translation**  
The registration for membership is complete, so you can use the service from now on.

**Explanation**  
The sentence refers to the state of the registration process. 完了 (かんりょう) is the most suitable word here, as it specifically indicates that a task or process has been fully completed. This aligns with the context of completing registration, allowing subsequent actions, such as using the service.

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect**  
- Answer 1: 決着（けっちゃく）means "settlement" or "conclusion" of a conflict or situation. It doesn’t fit here as it typically relates to resolving disputes, not completing a registration process.

questions.stem: 年を取って運動をしなくなると、筋肉がだんだん（　　　）いきます。
questions.expl:
**Correct Answer**  
Answer 4: 衰えて is correct. It means "to weaken" or "to decline."

**Question Translation**  
As you age and stop exercising, your muscles gradually weaken.

**Explanation**  
The sentence describes a scenario where muscles naturally weaken due to aging and a lack of exercise. The verb 衰える (おとろえる) means "to become weak" or "to decline," which perfectly aligns with the gradual weakening of muscle over time. This makes it the most appropriate choice given the context of aging and decreasing physical activity.

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect**  
- Answer 1: 潰れて (つぶれて) means "to be crushed" or "to collapse." It indicates a complete breakdown rather than a gradual weakening, making it unsuitable in describing a natural aging process for muscles.
- Answer 2: 欠けて (かけて) means "to be lacking" or "to be insufficient." While muscles may lack strength, this term doesn't specifically refer to a gradual decline. It's more about an absence or deficit rather than the process of weakening.
- Answer 3: 尽きて (つきて) means "to run out" or "to be exhausted." This implies that the muscles are completely finished, which is not accurate as the sentence refers to a gradual decline, not an exhaustion or depletion.

**Grammar/Vocabulary Note**  
Understanding how verbs are used to describe processes or states is crucial in Japanese. 衰える (おとろえる) is often used to describe a gradual weakening or diminishing over time, commonly in the context of health, skill, or capacity. Recognizing these nuances helps in selecting the appropriate verb that accurately describes changes in conditions or states.

**Question Translation**  
Since the time for the meeting was running low, the detailed explanation of the materials was omitted, and only the main points were explained.

**Explanation**  
In this context, the sentence involves omitting details due to limited time. 省略 (しょうりゃく) fits well because it means skipping over details to focus on the essentials, which aligns with the need to prioritize important points over exhaustive details when time is constrained.

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect**  
- Answer 1: 減量（げんりょう）means "weight loss" or "reduction in quantity." It doesn’t fit this context as it refers to physical reduction, not the omission of information.

**Grammar/Vocabulary Note**  
The term 省略 (しょうりゃく) is often used in both written and spoken Japanese to discuss the omission or abbreviation of information. questions.stem: この小説はフィクションだと（　　　）いたが、実際にあった話らしい。
questions.expl:
**Correct Answer**  
Answer 1: 思い込んで is correct. It means "to assume" or "to be under the impression."

**Question Translation**  
I was under the impression that this novel was fiction, but it seems it's actually a true story.

**Explanation**  
The sentence suggests that the speaker had a belief or assumption about the nature of the novel, which later turns out to be incorrect. 思い込む (おもいこむ) means to strongly believe or assume something, typically without sufficient evidence. This fits perfectly into the context where the person had a mistaken belief about the novel being fiction.

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect**  
- Answer 2: 思い起こして (おもいおこして) means "to recall" or "to remember." It suggests recalling something from memory, which doesn’t fit the context of initially believing something false about the story.
- Answer 3: 考え抜いて (かんがえぬいて) means "to think through" or "to consider thoroughly." This expression implies a deep, thorough consideration, not an assumption or impression about the novel being fiction.
- Answer 4: 考えついて (かんがえついて) means "to come up with" or "to think of." This suggests the act of generating an idea or solution, which doesn't align with having an incorrect belief about the novel.

**Grammar/Vocabulary Note**  
思い込む is a compound verb where 思う (to think) combines with 込む (to get into), capturing the notion of getting deeply fixed into one’s thought or assumption, often without challenging it. This is essential in understanding how people form and often maintain initial beliefs. Recognizing verb combinations like these is crucial for selecting the right context in sentences.

questions.stem: 薄める
opts: 私には難しすぎたので、コースのレベルを薄めた
部屋が暑かったので、エアコンをつけて温度を薄めた
スープがしょっぱかったので、水を加えて味を薄めた
うるさいと言われたので、テレビの音量を薄めた
questions.expl:
**Correct Answer**  
Answer 3 is correct.

**Word Translation**  
薄める（うすめる） — to dilute, to make something less strong/thin

**Correct Sentence Translation**  
The soup was salty, so I added water to dilute the flavor.

**Explanation**  
The word **薄める** means to make something less concentrated or intense, typically by adding something to it, like water. In this context, "味を薄めた" (diluted the flavor) is a natural usage, as it refers to adjusting the strength of the soup's taste.

**Other Options**

① 私には難しすぎたので、コースのレベルを薄めた。  
→ It was too difficult for me, so I diluted the course level.  
❌ Incorrect Usage  
"薄めた" is not used for abstract concepts like "course level." Instead, use "下げた" (lowered) or "易しくした" (made easier).

② 部屋が暑かったので、エアコンをつけて温度を薄めた。  
→ The room was hot, so I turned on the AC to dilute the temperature.  
❌ Incorrect Usage  
"薄めた" does not apply to temperature. More appropriate words include "下げた" (lowered) or "弱めた" (reduced).

④ うるさいと言われたので、テレビの音量を薄めた。  
→ I was told it was noisy, so I diluted the TV volume.  
❌ Incorrect Usage  
"薄めた" is not used for adjusting volume. Use "下げた" (lowered) or "小さくした" (made smaller).

**Usage Note**  
"薄める" is specifically used for tangible substances whose concentration or strength can be physically altered, such as liquids being diluted or colors lightened, but not for abstract ideas or any settings like temperature or volume levels.

questions.stem: 充実
opts: 今日の午後は雨の予報で、空には雲が充実
今はやりがいのある仕事ができて、毎日が充実

questions.expl:
**Correct Answer**  
Answer 2 is correct.

**Word Translation**  
充実（じゅうじつ） — fulfillment, richness, being satisfactorily complete

**Correct Sentence Translation**  
Now, I have a fulfilling job, so every day feels fulfilling.

**Explanation**  
The word **充実** is used to express a state of being full, satisfying, or enriched in a positive way. "毎日が充実している" (every day feels fulfilling) is a common expression in Japanese, especially when talking about personal satisfaction or richness of life.

**Other Options**

① 今日の午後は雨の予報で、空には雲が充実している。  
→ The forecast for this afternoon is rain, and the sky is full of clouds.  
❌ Incorrect Usage  
The word "充実" does not fit here, as it leans toward abstract or emotional fullness, not physical. A more appropriate choice would be "いっぱい" or "覆われている".

③ 喫茶店の中は、コーヒーのにおいが充実している。  
→ The coffee shop is full of the smell of coffee.  
🔶 Awkward Usage  
While you might think of a space being full of aroma, "充実" is not generally used with scents. "漂っている" or "満ちている" are more natural for describing pervasive aromas.

④ 計画を実行するためには、まだ問題が充実している。  
→ There are still problems in abundance for executing the plan.  
❌ Incorrect Usage  
"充実" implies a positive richness or completeness, not problems. "存在している" or "残っている" would be correct in this context.

**Usage Note**  
"充実" is often paired with activities, feelings, or lifestyles where there is a sense of completeness and fulfillment. It does not align well with descriptions of physical quantities, scents, or problems.

opts: 次回のセミナーの開催日はまだ鮮明
できそうにない仕事は鮮明
B社の製品のほうが性能が鮮明
あのときの出来事は今でも鮮明
questions.expl:
**Correct Answer**  
Answer 4 is correct.

**Word Translation**  
鮮明（せんめい） — vivid, clear, distinct

**Correct Sentence Translation**  
I still vividly remember the events of that time.

**Explanation**  
The word **鮮明** conveys clarity and vividness, often used to describe memories, images, or impressions. "鮮明に覚えている" (vividly remember) is a natural and common expression in Japanese for emphasizing the clarity of a memory.

**Other Options**

① 次回のセミナーの開催日はまだ__鮮明__に決まっていない。  
→ The date for the next seminar hasn’t been clearly decided yet.  
❌ Incorrect Usage  
"鮮明" is not used to describe decision clarity. Words like "はっきり" or "明確に" would be more appropriate in this context.

② できそうにない仕事は__鮮明__に断ったほうがいい。  
→ It's better to clearly refuse work that seems impossible.  
❌ Incorrect Usage  
"鮮明" is not suitable to describe the manner of refusal. Using "はっきり" or "きっぱり" would be more natural.

③ B社の製品のほうが性能が__鮮明__に優れている。  
→ Company B's products are distinctly superior in performance.  
🔶 Awkward Usage  
While "鮮明に" can denote distinctness, it sounds slightly off when describing product performance. "はっきりと" is a more typical choice for clarity in comparisons.

**Usage Note**  
"鮮明" is typically used with words like "記憶" (memory), "印象" (impression), or "画像" (image), to denote vividness or clarity in perceivable attributes. It is not appropriately paired with actions or decisions, which require clarity rather than vividness.

포인트: 鮮明=(기억·영상이) 또렷함.

questions.stem: ふもと
questions.expl:
**Correct Answer**  
Answer 3 is correct.

**Word Translation**  
ふもと — foothill, the base of a mountain

**Correct Sentence Translation**  
Let's park the car at the base of the mountain and start climbing from there.

**Explanation**  
The word **ふもと** refers to the lower region or base of a mountain, an area where the mountain starts. "山のふもと" (base of the mountain) is a natural and typical expression in Japanese, often used in contexts related to hiking, geography, or nature.

**Other Options**

② あのビルの__ふもと__に、新しいお店ができるらしい。  
→ It seems a new store will open at the base of that building.  
🔶 Awkward Usage  
"ふもと" specifically refers to the base of natural structures, like mountains or hills, not man-made structures like buildings. Instead, "ふもと" would be replaced with "下" (under or underneath) to describe a building.

① 明日、駅の__ふもと__で[池田|いけだ]さんと会う約束をした。  
→ I’ve arranged to meet Ikeda-san tomorrow at the foothill of the station.  
❌ Incorrect Usage  
A train station doesn't have a "ふもと" since it is not a mountain or natural elevation. The appropriate term here might be "前" (in front) or "近く" (nearby).

④ ドアの__ふもと__に[猫|ねこ]がいて、開けることができない。  
→ There’s a cat at the base of the door, so I can't open it.  
❌ Incorrect Usage  
"ふもと" does not apply to inanimate objects or flat surfaces like doors. "前" or "下" (front or below) would correctly convey the cat's position near the door.

**Usage Note**  
"ふもと" is specifically used for geographical features, such as mountains or large hills. It implies the lowermost area of a natural elevation, not suitable for describing man-made or flat objects.

questions.stem: 定年
opts: この乗り物は子ども向けのため、10歳が定年
questions.expl:
**Correct Answer**  
Answer 1 is correct.

**Word Translation**  
定年（ていねん） — retirement age

**Correct Sentence Translation**  
In my company, the retirement age is 60, so I will retire in half a year.

**Explanation**  
The word **定年** refers specifically to the age at which a person typically retires from work, often predefined by a company's policy or national regulations. The phrase "60歳が定年" (retirement age is 60) is a common and natural expression.

**Other Options**

② この乗り物は子ども向けのため、10歳が__定年__になっている。  
→ This ride is for children, so the retirement age is set at 10 years.  
❌ Incorrect Usage  
"定年" is used for employment retirement, not for age restrictions on activities or rides. More appropriate phrases might be "対象年齢が10歳まで" or "年齢制限".

③ この国では、__定年__の20歳になると選挙で投票することができる。  
→ In this country, upon reaching the retirement age of 20, one can vote in elections.  
❌ Incorrect Usage  
"定年" is incorrect because it refers to retirement, not the age of majority. The phrase should be "成人年齢" (age of majority) or plain "20歳".

④ 犬の__定年__は一般的に10歳から15歳の間だといわれている。  
→ A dog's retirement age is generally said to be between 10 and 15 years.  
❌ Incorrect Usage  
Animals do not retire in the way humans do. Use terms like "平均寿命" (average lifespan) or "シニア年齢" (senior age).

**Usage Note**  
"定年" is specifically used for the retirement age in a professional context and is not applicable to age limits, legal ages, or animal ages. It signifies the end of an individual's full-time working life, leading to retirement.

When I first started attending the swimming class, I couldn't even put my face in the water because I was scared, but now I love swimming.

**Explanation**  
The correct answer, "さえ," highlights an extreme or unexpected example within a situation. In this context, the person couldn't handle the basic action of putting their face in the water due to fear, which emphasizes their initial struggle with swimming. It's used to stress the difficulty even with the simplest things when they began.

- Answer 1: なら (meaning "if") does not fit grammatically in the context as it usually introduces a conditional clause, which doesn't match the sentence's structure describing past experience.

**Grammar/Vocabulary Note**  
The particle "さえ" is a focus marker used for emphasis and is often paired with negative forms to show something that is normally easy or trivial was challenging or unachievable. Understanding its use is crucial for recognizing how it shifts focus and adds emphasis in Japanese sentences.

questions.stem: この図書館には、借りている本を全部（　　　）、ほかの本が借りられないという規則がある。
questions.expl:
**Correct Answer**  
Answer 4: 返してからでないと is correct. It means "unless you return (the books)".

**Question Translation**  
In this library, there is a rule that unless you return all the books you have borrowed, you cannot borrow other books.

**Explanation**  
The phrase 返してからでないと is used to express a condition that must be fulfilled before another action can occur. It translates to "unless you return," indicating that returning the books is a prerequisite for being able to borrow more books. This structure fits well with the context of the sentence, which describes a rule (regulation) in the library.

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect**  
- Answer 1: 返したすえに means "after having returned". This implies a sequence of events, but it doesn't clearly communicate the necessity of returning the books before borrowing more. It suggests completion without the conditional aspect needed here.
  
- Answer 2: 返したとはいえ means "although (you) returned". This introduces a contrast or contradiction and would indicate an unexpected result after returning the books, which doesn’t fit the context of a straightforward rule.
  
- Answer 3: 返してはじめて means "only after returning". While it indicates a precondition, it implies an exclusive realization or understanding after the action, which is not the intended meaning of enforcing a strict rule in this context.

**Grammar/Vocabulary Note**  
The phrase 〜からでないと is a common grammatical structure used to indicate that one action must be completed before another can occur. It essentially marks something as a prerequisite, similar to "unless/until" in English, and is often used in rules or instructions. Understanding this structure is essential for interpreting sentences that involve conditional prerequisites.

Answer 2: やりたがらないのなら is correct. It means "if he doesn't seem to want to do [it]."

**Question Translation**  
My wife insists on making our son learn the piano, but I think it's not necessary to force him if he doesn't really want to.

**Explanation**  
The phrase やりたがらないのなら (yari tagaranai no nara) translates to "if he doesn’t want to do [it]." This solution is appropriate because it directly addresses the son's lack of desire, which aligns with the speaker's belief about not forcing him.

- Answer 3: やってほしくないのに (yatte hoshikunai no ni) translates as "even though I don't want him to do [it]." This focuses on the speaker’s desire rather than the son's, which contradicts the context focused on the son's preference.
  
- Answer 4: やってもはじまらないのに (yatte mo hajimaranai no ni) means "even though nothing will begin if he does [it]." This option introduces a new concept unrelated to the scenario, as it highlights ineffectiveness rather than the son's willingness.

**Grammar/Vocabulary Note**  
- たがる (tagaru) is a verb suffix used to indicate what someone else wants to do. It is used when observing or inferring the desires of others, not one's own. In this context, やりたがらない (yaritagarai) shows the son's disinterest explicitly.

When I started this research, there were many critical opinions questioning whether there was any meaning in researching such a thing, but recently it has slowly gained some recognition.

**Explanation**  
The phrase "あるのかというような" is used to express a doubtful or questioning perspective over whether something holds true, in this context, whether the research has meaning. The structure "〜のかというような" is often employed to convey uncertainty or skepticism about a statement.

**Grammar/Vocabulary Note**  
The structure "〜のかというような" is used to express a tentative or doubtful perspective, questioning the existence or validity of something. questions.stem: 腕のけがはまだ完全に（　　　）が、日常生活には困らなくなった。
questions.expl:
Correct Answer
Answer 4 is correct. It means “hasn’t exactly healed / isn’t completely healed.”

Question Translation
“My arm injury hasn’t completely healed yet, but I’ve stopped having trouble in everyday life.”

Explanation
**〜わけではない** softens/partially negates a statement: “it’s not the case that ….” 「完全に治ったわけではない」 fits the contrast with 「が、日常生活には困らなくなった」—not fully healed, yet life is no longer inconvenient.

Why Other Options Are Incorrect
1. 治りようがない — “there’s no way to heal (incurable).” → Too strong/absolute and contradicts “no longer inconvenient.”
2. 治らないでもない — “it’s not that it won’t heal (it might heal).” → Talks about *possibility*, not current condition; doesn’t match the contrastive sentence.
3. 治ったにすぎない — “it has only healed, nothing more.” → States it **has healed**, which clashes with 「まだ完全に…」 and the intended partial negation.

Grammar/Vocabulary Note
• **〜わけではない**: partial negation/qualification.
• **〜ようがない**: “no means/way to …,” absolute impossibility.
• **〜ないでもない**: double-negative to allow possibility.
• **〜にすぎない**: “no more than/merely,” downplays but affirms the fact.

What is being required of employees?

questions.expl:
**Correct Answer**  
Answer 1: わかり合えないと思うところから、お互いの理解が始まる。  
This is correct. It means, "Understanding each other begins from the point of thinking that we cannot understand each other."

**Question Translation**  
What does the author think about the relationship between parents and children?

**Explanation**  
The passage suggests that realizing the limits in understanding each other (親子はもっとも身近でありながら、ときにもっとも遠くなってしまう存在) can be the first step toward truly trying to understand one another. The author reflects on personal experience, acknowledging a distance when recognizing they cannot fully understand their mother (わかり合えない), but doesn't see this realization as reducing affection or warmth. Instead, the author argues that acknowledging this gap is the first step towards understanding (むしろ「わかり合えない」とわかることは相手を理解しようとするための最初の一歩). Thus, Answer 1 directly aligns with the author's thoughts on understanding starting from recognizing limits.

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect**  
- Answer 2: わかり合えないということに、お互いが気づくのは難しい (It's difficult for both to realize that they do not understand each other). This option implies difficulty in mutual realization, which isn't emphasized by the author. The passage focuses more on the realization itself being significant, rather than its difficulty.
- Answer 3: わかり合うためには、一定の距離を保つことが大切だ (Keeping a certain distance is important to understand each other). While the author mentions a distance, they do not advocate maintaining it for understanding. The passage emphasizes understanding through the acknowledgment of inability to fully understand, not by maintaining distance.
- Answer 4: 身近な存在だからこそ、いつかはわかり合えるものだ (Because we are close, we will understand each other someday). This is contrary to the author's realization that closeness does not guarantee understanding, and instead, recognizing a lack of complete understanding is crucial for real understanding.

**Grammar/Vocabulary Note**  
- "わかり合えない" is a key expression, literally meaning “cannot understand each other,” playing a central role in the passage’s theme about beginning understanding from recognizing limitations.
- The word "否めない" means "cannot deny," indicating the inevitable realization the author faced, reinforcing the theme of recognition rather than denial.

questions.stem: 必ずしも良いことではないとあるが、なぜか。
opts: 予想しなかったことにうまく対応できないかもしれないから

questions.expl:
**Correct Answer**  
Answer 1: 予想しなかったことにうまく対応できないかもしれないから is correct. It means "because you might not be able to handle unexpected things well."

**Question Translation**  
"But it says it's not always a good thing. Why is that?"

**Explanation**  
The passage explains that not feeling anxious or tense in a new environment is not always good because it can lead to unexpected failures. Being too relaxed might make one overlook potential risks or fail to prepare for unusual situations. Answer 1 directly addresses this concern by stating the inability to cope with unexpected events, which aligns with the passage's main argument about the risks of being too comfortable in unfamiliar settings.

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect**  
- Answer 2: これまでと同じような失敗をする可能性があるから ("because there is a possibility of making the same mistakes as before") is incorrect. The passage doesn't mention repeating past mistakes as a risk of lacking anxiety in new environments.
- Answer 3: これまでのやり方を周囲に押しつけてしまうから ("because you might impose your old ways on those around you") is incorrect. The passage does not discuss imposing previous methods on others as a potential issue.
- Answer 4: いつまでも新しい環境に慣れることができないから ("because you can never get used to a new environment") is incorrect. The passage specifically talks about being too at ease without anxiety, rather than struggling to adapt.

**Grammar/Vocabulary Note**  
必ずしも (かならずしも) is a useful expression meaning "not always" or "not necessarily." It is often used to indicate that something is not absolabrace or unconditionally true. Understanding this nuance helps to comprehend the passage's point about the mixed blessings of feeling too comfortable in a new setting.

questions.expl:
**Correct Answer**
Answer 3 is correct. It means: "When you feel anxiety or tension, value that feeling and act without hesitation."

**Question Translation**
"Which option agrees with the writer’s view?"

**Explanation**
The author says anxiety/tension function as a safety device and, when felt, we should trust that inner signal and *without overthinking* focus on what we can do today. The writer also warns that **not** feeling anxiety in a new environment isn’t necessarily good and that caution born from anxiety helps us prepare and respond carefully. Thus, valuing the feeling and proceeding with focused action matches the passage.

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect**
1. "To avoid feeling anxiety or tension, just keep calm and focus on what you can do now." — ❌ The author doesn’t tell us to *avoid* those feelings; they’re useful signals and shouldn’t be suppressed.

The passage discusses how the process of interpreting a novel involves personal imagination. When a novel is adapted into a film, each reader's mental image of the story may differ from the director's interpretation. The passage states that it's natural for people to disagree on the film's portrayal because the original work allows for unique, personal interpretations. Section A mentions that the inability to remember is not due to inherently poor memory, but rather unrefined memorization techniques. Similarly, Section B states that forgetting is not a result of poor memory, but because the memorization method was incorrect.

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect**  
- Answer 1: 暗記したあとに復習することで、記憶力が上がる. While revisiting memorized content helps strengthen memory, only Section B specifically discusses it. It is not a common idea shared between both sections.
  
- Answer 3: 暗記をし続けても、記憶力は強化されない. This states that continual memorization does not reinforce memory. Neither passage directly supports this claim. Both sections focus on improving methods rather than questioning the value of continuous memorization.

- Answer 4: 暗記に対して苦手意識があると、記憶力もよくならない. This suggests feeling inadequate about memorization affects memory ability. This point is not supported by both sections. Section A touches on this sentiment but does not conclude that it affects memory capability.

**Grammar/Vocabulary Note**  
None of the answers or passages require specific grammar or vocabulary notes beyond the normal level of the JLPT test-takers' understanding. However, it is important to understand the words 記憶力 (きおくりょく), meaning "memory capacity" or "memory capability," and 工夫 (くふう), meaning "device," "scheme," or "way," to understand the emphasis on methods.

opts: ＡもＢも、さまざまな方法を試しながら自分に合った方法を見つけて暗記するといいと述べている。
ＡもＢも、内容に応じて、朝か夜かを変えながら暗記するといいと述べている。
Ａは複数の感覚を使って暗記するといいと述べ、Ｂは夜寝る前に重点的に暗記するといいと述べている。

questions.expl:
**Correct Answer**  
Answer 3: Ａは複数の感覚を使って暗記するといいと述べ、Ｂは夜寝る前に重点的に暗記するといいと述べている。 This answer is correct. It means "A suggests using multiple senses for memorization, and B suggests concentrating on memorization before going to sleep at night."

**Question Translation**  
What advice do A and B give regarding methods of memorization?

**Explanation**  
Based on the provided passage, the text associated with A suggests enhancing memorization by engaging multiple senses, such as saying information out loud (auditory) and writing it down (kinesthetic) to stimulate the brain from various angles, which can improve memory retention. This aligns with the part of Answer 3 stating "複数の感覚を使って暗記するといい" (suggests using multiple senses). The section about B highlights the timing of memorization, particularly focusing on the benefits of studying shortly before sleeping to enable better organization and retention of knowledge during sleep. This supports the part of Answer 3 stating "夜寝る前に重点的に暗記するといい" (suggests concentrating on memorization before sleep at night).

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect**  
- Answer 1: This option suggests that both A and B advise trying various methods to find what suits the individual best, but the passages do not explicitly discuss experimenting with different methods or individual customization.
- Answer 2: This option implies that A and B both suggest changing memorization time based on content, which is incorrect as A does not discuss timing, only B does.
- Answer 4: This suggests A focuses on vocal and written methods, and B advises finding one's own best time for memorization. While partially true, it misrepresents B, as B specifically recommends nighttime memorization.

**Grammar/Vocabulary Note**  
- "複数の感覚" (ふくすうのかんかく) means “multiple senses,” emphasizing the idea of utilizing more than the visual sense for better memorization effectiveness.
- “重点的に" (じゅうてんてきに) means “focus on” or “concentrate on,” highlighting the targeted advice of nighttime study for better retention.

According to the author, what do managers and leaders want their subordinates and juniors to do?

**Explanation**  
The passage indicates that many managers and leaders expect their subordinates and juniors to tackle issues independently and to think about their next steps. More specifically, they want their team to consider both "what" needs to be done and "how" it should be done without constantly seeking guidance. **Correct Answer**  
Answer 2: それぞれの個性や能力に応じた指導をすること is correct. It means "Providing guidance tailored to each individual's characteristics and abilities."

**Question Translation**  
According to the author, what is difficult in guiding mid-level and mid-career recruits?

**Explanation**  
The passage focuses on the difficulty of training mid-level employees and mid-career recruits because these individuals already possess basic job performance skills, experience, and pride. This means that managers must tailor their guidance according to the unique characteristics and abilities of each person. This requires acknowledging each individual's differences in personality and skills, which makes the guidance complex. Therefore, the correct answer is about instructing each employee according to their individual traits and abilities.

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect**  
- Answer 1: 多くの時間とエネルギーを使って、仕事を細かく教えること translates to "Spending a lot of time and energy teaching the job in detail." This is more applicable to new employees, who require detailed teaching and repeated feedback.
  
- Answer 3: 前の仕事の経験を生かせるような指導をすること translates to "Guidance that allows one to make use of experience from previous jobs." While past experience may be relevant, the passage does not specifically highlight this as the primary difficulty in guiding mid-level and mid-career hires.
  
- Answer 4: プライドを傷つけずに、基本的なことを教えること translates to "Teaching basic things without hurting pride." Although the text mentions respecting their pride, it emphasizes the need to adjust guidance to their unique traits rather than focusing solely on protecting their pride.

**Grammar/Vocabulary Note**  
- 中堅社員（ちゅうけんしゃいん）means "mid-level employee," indicating someone who has been in the workforce long enough to be significantly experienced yet not necessarily in top management.
- 本文の「考慮」（こうりょ）means taking into account or considering, crucial for understanding how managers need to plan their mentoring by considering individual differences.

**Correct Answer**  
Answer 3: 部下や後輩を育てることで気づきが得られ、自らも成長できる。 It means "By nurturing subordinates and juniors, one can gain insights and also grow themselves."

**Question Translation**  
Regarding the people in teaching roles, which opinion aligns with the author’s views?  

**Explanation**  
The passage discusses the difficulties and rewards of teaching subordinates and juniors. It emphasizes how teaching can lead to insights about one’s own understanding and help improve the teacher's knowledge and skills. This aligns with the statement that nurturing others helps both gain insights and allows personal growth, which is why Answer 3 is the best fit. 

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect**  
- **Answer 1**: 部下や後輩の指導では、相手を理解することに時間をかけるべきだ。 This suggests that understanding the other person is where time should be spent. However, the passage focuses more on the learning and growth of the one who teaches, rather than allocating time specifically on understanding others.
  
- **Answer 2**: 部下や後輩から学ぶ姿勢があれば、自分の知識や技術が向上する。 This option assumes a learning stance and personal improvement from subordinates and juniors themselves, which is not the main thematic focus of the passage. The text is more about the process and benefit earned by teaching others.
  
- **Answer 4**: 自身が成長するために、多くの部下や後輩を指導したほうがいい。 This suggests that in order to grow oneself, one should instruct many subordinates and juniors, implying a quantitative approach. The passage instead suggests that it is about gaining insights and growth through the act of nurturing itself, not the amount.
  
**Grammar/Vocabulary Note**  
The passage employs the verb "育てる" (そだてる) which means "to nurture" or "to raise." It's used to describe both the act of teaching subordinates and the resulting personal development. Recognizing how this term is tied with personal growth is essential for choosing the correct answer.

M： 私わたしは最近さいきん、棚たなとか椅子いすとか趣味しゅみでいろいろな家具かぐを作つくっています。近頃ちかごろは手頃てごろな値段ねだんで買かえる店みせも多おおいですが、自分じぶんが本当ほんとうに欲ほしい家具かぐってなかなかないんですよね。その点てん、自分じぶんで作つくれば考かんがえた通とおりの[デザイン]で作つくれるでしょう？頭あたまに浮うかんだ[アイデア]を自分じぶんの手てで家具かぐとして完成かんせいさせていくっていう過程かていがたまらないんです。仕事しごとがあるので集中しゅうちゅうして一気いっきに作つくることは難むずかしいし、うまくできないと[ストレス]になることもあるんですけど、やっぱり楽たのしいですね。

俳優はいゆうは家具かぐを作つくることのどんなところに魅力みりょくを感かんじると言いっていますか。
questions.translation_en:
On the radio, an actor is talking. What does the actor say is appealing about making furniture?

M: Recently, I’ve been making various pieces of furniture like shelves and chairs as a hobby. These days, there are many stores where you can buy affordable furniture, but it’s hard to find something I truly want. In that sense, when I make it myself, I can create it exactly as I imagine it. The process of turning an idea that comes to mind into a completed piece of furniture with my own hands is incredibly satisfying. It’s hard to focus and make things all at once since I have work, and sometimes it’s stressful when it doesn’t go well, but it’s still fun.

What does the actor say is appealing about making furniture?
questions.expl_ko: 정답: 2번 (自分のアイデアを形にすること). 근거: 음성 「頭に浮かんだアイデアを自分の手で家具として完成させていくっていう過程がたまらないんです」 — 아이디어를 형태로 만드는 과정에 매료. 오답: 1. 싸게 만드는 것은 언급 없음. 2. 정답. 3. 집중 시간은 「集中して一気に作ることは難しい」 부정. 4. 스트레스 해소는 「ストレスになることもある」 오히려 반대. 포인트: 「~がたまらない」=~이 너무 좋다. 매력의 핵심 지점.

陸上競技りくじょうきょうぎの大会たいかいでアナウンサーが選手せんしゅにインタビューしています。選手せんしゅはどうして今日きょう、勝かつことができたと言いっていますか。

M： 女子じょし5000メートル優勝ゆうしょうの酒井さかい選手せんしゅです。おめでとうございます。今日きょうの試合しあい、ご自身じしんで振ふり返かえっていかがでしたか？
F： そうですね。最後さいごはきつかったんですけど、思おもい切きってスピードを上あげて、それが効きいたんだと思おもいます。もっと早はやい段階だんかいで前まえに出でて自分じぶんのペースを維持いじできればよかったんですけど、今回こんかいの試合しあいは風かぜが強つよかったのでスピードを落おとさずにいる自信じしんがなくて・・・。それで途中とちゅうまでは他ほかの選手せんしゅについていきました。次つぎの試合しあいは早はやめに先頭せんとうを取とりに行いきたいです。

選手せんしゅはどうして今日きょう、勝かつことができたと言いっていますか。
questions.translation_en:
At a track-and-field meet, an announcer is interviewing an athlete. Why does the athlete say she was able to win today?

M: This is Sakai, the winner of the women’s 5000 meters. Congratulations! How do you look back on today’s race?
F: Well, the end was tough, but I decided to go for it, increased my speed, and I think that worked. It would’ve been better if I had gone to the front earlier and maintained my own pace, but since it was windy today, I wasn’t confident I could keep my speed. So I stayed with the other runners until partway through. Next time, I want to take the lead earlier.

Why does the athlete say she was able to win today?
questions.expl_ko: 정답: 1번 (最後に十分加速できたから). 근거: 음성 「最後はきつかったんですけど、思い切ってスピードを上げて、それが効いたんだと思います」 — 마지막 가속이 주효. 오답: 1. 정답. 2. 자기 페이스 유지는 「維持できればよかった」 못한 일. 3. 도중 속도 떨어뜨림은 「他の選手についていきました」 추격이지 감속 아님. 4. 일찍 선두는 「次の試合は早めに先頭を取りに行きたい」 다음 목표. 포인트: 「~が効いた」=~이 효과를 봤다. 승인 표현.

questions.script_html:
大学だいがくで女おんなの学生がくせいと男おとこの学生がくせいが国際協力こくさいきょうりょくの勉強会べんきょうかいについて話はなしています。男おとこの学生がくせいは勉強会べんきょうかいで良よくなかったことは何なんだと言いっていますか。

F： 加藤かとうくん、今日きょうの勉強会べんきょうかいお疲つかれ様さま。進行役しんこうやく、どうだった？
M： 参加者さんかしゃの反応はんのう、良よかったと思おもうよ。いつもは論文ろんぶんを読よみ合あうのが中心ちゅうしんで、卒業そつぎょうした先輩せんぱいを講師こうしに呼よぶのは初はじめてだったけど、海外かいがいボランティアのいろんな話はなしが聞きけたし、うまくいったんじゃない？
F： そうだね。講師こうしは一人ひとりじゃなくて何人なんにんか呼よんだほうがよかったかな？
M： いや、一人ひとりの先輩せんぱいの話はなしだからこそ、じっくり話はなしが聞きけたんだと思おもうよ。
F： 借かりた教室きょうしつが広ひろすぎて意見交換いけんこうかんがしにくくなるかなって心配しんぱいだったけど。
M： そんなことなかったよ。質問しつもんもたくさん出でたし。うーん、始はじまる時間じかんはもう少すこし余裕よゆうを持もって参加さんかできる設定せっていにしたほうが良よかったと思おもうよ。授業じゅぎょうが延のびたとかで遅おくれてくる人ひともいたから。
F： 確たしかに。
M： いつもは事前じぜんに論文ろんぶんに目めを通とおさなきゃいけないけど、今回こんかいは参加者さんかしゃの負担ふたんもなくて、たまにはそれもいいかなって。
F： そうだね。

男おとこの学生がくせいは勉強会べんきょうかいで良よくなかったことは何なんだと言いっていますか。
questions.translation_en:
At university, a female and a male student are talking about a study meeting on international cooperation. What does the male student say was not good about the meeting?

F: Kato, good job today. How was it as the facilitator?
M: I think the participants’ reactions were good. We usually focus on reading papers together, and it was our first time inviting a graduate as a speaker, but we heard various stories about overseas volunteering, so I think it went well.
F: Do you think it would’ve been better to invite several speakers instead of just one?
M: No, precisely because it was one senior, we could listen carefully.
F: I was worried the borrowed classroom was too big and might make discussion difficult.
M: That wasn’t a problem. There were plenty of questions. Hmm… I think the start time should have been set so people could come with a little more leeway, because some arrived late due to classes running long.
F: True.
M: Usually we have to read papers beforehand, but this time there wasn’t much burden on participants, and that’s fine once in a while.
F: Yeah.

What does the male student say was not good about the study meeting?
questions.expl_ko: 정답: 3번 (開始時間が早かったこと). 근거: 음성 「始まる時間はもう少し余裕を持って参加できる設定にしたほうが良かった…授業が延びたとかで遅れてくる人もいたから」 — 시작 시각이 너무 일러 지각자 발생. 오답: 1. 강사 한 명은 「一人の先輩の話だからこそ、じっくり話が聞けた」 오히려 좋았다. 2. 교실이 넓은 것도 「そんなことなかったよ」 문제 아님. 3. 정답. 4. 사전 자료 없음은 평가 외. 포인트: 「~ほうが良かった」=~ 쪽이 좋았을 것. 아쉬운 점 지적.

questions.script_html:
会社かいしゃの人事部じんじぶの会議かいぎで部長ぶちょうが話はなしています。

男おとこ：えー、今年度こんねんどは実務経験じつむけいけんのある方かたの採用さいようを大幅おおはばに増ふやす予定よていですが、応募者数おうぼしゃすうがかなり多おおいのでしっかり選考せんこうしてください。面接めんせつでは専門的せんもんてきな知識ちしきや経験けいけんの有無うむはもちろんのこと、いろいろな環境かんきょうに柔軟じゅうなんに対応たいおうできる力ちからがあるかを見みてください。それから、応募者おうぼしゃがわが社しゃでの活躍かつやくをどのようにイメージできているかという点てんも見みてください。

部長ぶちょうは何なにについて話はなしていますか。
1. 採用さいようの面接めんせつで重視じゅうしすること
2. 今年ことしの応募者おうぼしゃの特徴とくちょう
3. 採用人数さいようにんずうを増ふやした理由りゆう
4. 入社後にゅうしゃごの新人社員しんじんしゃいんの活躍かつやく
questions.translation_en:
In a company’s personnel department meeting, the manager is speaking.

M: This year, we plan to significantly increase the hiring of people with practical experience, but since there are quite a lot of applicants, please make sure to select them carefully. In the interviews, of course, check their specialized knowledge and experience, but also see whether they can flexibly adapt to various environments. Also, please see how the applicants imagine themselves being active in our company.

What is the manager talking about?
1. What to emphasize in hiring interviews
2. Characteristics of this year’s applicants
3. The reason for increasing the number of hires
4. The performance of new employees after joining the company.
questions.expl_ko: 정답: 1번 (採用の面接で重視すること). 근거: 음성 「面接では専門的な知識や経験の有無はもちろんのこと、いろいろな環境に柔軟に対応できる力があるかを見てください…活躍をどのようにイメージできているかという点も見てください」 — 면접에서 볼 점들. 오답: 1. 정답. 2. 응모자 특징은 「多いので」 한 마디만. 3. 채용 증원 이유는 단순 배경. 4. 입사 후 활약은 면접에서 그릴 수 있는지 평가일 뿐. 포인트: 「~はもちろんのこと…も見てください」 중점 사항 나열.

questions.script_html:
ラジオで女おんなの人ひとが話はなしています。

女おんな：健康にいいと言われるハチミツは古ふるくから人々ひとびとに愛あいされてきました。西洋せいようでは2000年ねん以上前まえの書物しょもつに当時とうじの人ひとがハチミツを食たべていた記録きろくを見みることができます。また、西洋せいようのある神話しんわの中なかにもハチミツの作つくり方かたを教おしえたとされる神様かみさまが登場とうじょうします。
日本にほんでは8世紀せいきの書物しょもつにハチミツに関かんする記録きろくがありますが、ハチミツは長ながい間あいだ一部いちぶの人ひとしか口くちにできない貴重きちょうなものでした。明治めいじになると育そだてやすいとされる西洋蜜蜂せいようみつばちという種類しゅるいの蜂はちが輸入ゆにゅうされ、ハチミツが採とりやすくなったことで一般いっぱんの人ひとの間あいだでも一気いっきに普及ふきゅうしたのです。

女おんなの人ひとは、何なにについて話はなしていますか。
1. ハチミツをテーマにした物語ものがたり
2. ハチミツに含ふくまれる栄養えいよう
3. ハチミツの採とり方かた
4. 食料しょくりょうとしてのハチミツの歴史れきし
questions.translation_en:
A woman is talking on the radio.

F: Honey, which is said to be good for health, has been loved by people since ancient times. In the West, records from over 2,000 years ago show that people at that time ate honey. In some Western myths, there are even gods said to have taught how to make honey. In Japan, there are records about honey in writings from the 8th century, but for a long time, it was a precious item that only a few people could consume. In the Meiji era, when the Western honeybee, known to be easy to raise, was imported, it became easier to harvest honey, and it quickly spread among the general public.

What is the woman talking about?
1. Stories themed around honey
2. Nutrients contained in honey
3. How to collect honey
4. The history of honey as a food.
questions.expl_ko: 정답: 4번 (食料としてのハチミツの歴史). 근거: 음성 「2000年以上前の書物に…食べていた記録」「8世紀の書物にハチミツに関する記録」「明治になると…一気に普及した」 — 시대별 식용 꿀의 역사. 오답: 1. 신화 속 신은 한 예시일 뿐. 2. 영양 정보는 「健康にいいと言われる」 첫머리뿐. 3. 채집법은 「採りやすくなった」 한 줄. 4. 정답. 포인트: 「古くから~明治になると」 시간 흐름으로 역사 서술.

questions.script_html:
テレビでアナウンサーの男おとこの人ひとと絵本えほんの出版社しゅっぱんしゃの人ひとが話はなしています。

男おとこ：今日きょうは子供こども向けの本ほんの出版社しゅっぱんしゃ、さくら出版しゅっぱんの山田やまださんにお話はなしを伺うかがいます。さいきん、自分のために絵本えほんを購入こうにゅうする大人おとなが増ふえているそうですね。
女おんな：はい。絵本えほんは子供こどもでもわかるシンプルな言葉ことばで書かかれていますが、大人おとなが読よんでも心こころに響ひびくものがあるようです。あたたかなイラストや、心こころにまっすぐ届とどく言葉ことばで描えがかれた絵本えほんは、疲つかれた心こころをリラックスさせる効果こうかがあるという声こえが聞きかれます。
男おとこ：なるほど。ページ数ページすうも少すくなく、短時間たんじかんで読よめるというのも忙いそがしい大人おとなにとっては手てに取とりやすい理由りゆうの一ひとつなのかもしれませんね。
女おんな：ええ。いままでは絵本えほんというと子供こどもに読よんで聞きかせるものと思われがちでしたが、大人おとなでも十分じゅうぶんに楽たのしめるんだなと感かんじています。

出版社しゅっぱんしゃの人ひとは、何なにについて話はなしていますか。
1. 大人おとなにとっての絵本えほんの魅力みりょく
2. 大人おとなに選えらばれる絵本えほんのテーマ
3. 親子おやこで絵本えほんを読よむことのメリット
4. 絵本えほんが子供こどもに与あたえる影響えいきょう
questions.translation_en:
On TV, a male announcer and a representative from a picture book publisher are talking.

M: Today, we’re talking with Yamada from Sakura Publishing, a publisher of children’s books. Recently, it seems that more adults are buying picture books for themselves.
F: Yes. Picture books are written in simple language that even children can understand, but they also resonate with adults. Warm illustrations and direct, heartfelt words in these books are said to have a relaxing effect on tired hearts.
M: I see. With fewer pages and being easy to read in a short time, that might be another reason they’re appealing to busy adults.
F: Yes. Picture books used to be thought of as something to read to children, but I feel that adults can also enjoy them fully.

What is the publisher talking about?
1. The appeal of picture books for adults
2. Themes of picture books chosen by adults
3. Benefits of parents reading picture books with their children
4. Effects of picture books on children.
questions.expl_ko: 정답: 1번 (大人にとっての絵本の魅力). 근거: 음성 「大人が読んでも心に響くものがあるようです…疲れた心をリラックスさせる効果がある…大人にとっては手に取りやすい理由」 — 어른에게 그림책이 갖는 매력. 오답: 1. 정답. 2. 선택되는 주제는 다루지 않음. 3. 부모 자식 함께 읽기는 「子供に読んで聞かせるもの」 과거 인식으로만 언급. 4. 출판 동향이 주제 아님. 포인트: 「~に響く」=~에 와닿다. 「手に取りやすい」 매력 키워드.

questions.script_html:
講演会こうえんかいで映画監督えいがかんとくが話はなしています。

男おとこ：ぼくは子供こどものころから将来しょうらい、映画製作えいがせいさくの仕事しごとがしたくて、自分なりにさまざまな映画えいがのストーリー展開てんかいを研究けんきゅうし、いまの[スタイル]に行いきつきました。ぼくがオリジナルの映画えいがの構成こうせいを考かんがえるときは3つの要素ようそで物語ものがたりを展開てんかいさせます。
まず最初さいしょに問題もんだいの提示ていじ。つまり、何なにか困こまったことが起おきたりして解決かいけつすべきことを示しめします。そして主人公しゅじんこうが問題解決もんだいかいけつに向むかう中なかで予想外よそうがいの展開てんかいがあって、最終的さいしゅうてきに問題もんだいが解決かいけつする。その過程かていで主人公しゅじんこうを成長せいちょうさせるんです。恋愛れんあいものでも歴史れきしものでも、それは共通きょうつうしていますね。

映画監督えいがかんとくは何なにについて話はなしていますか。
1. 最近さいきんの映画研究えいがけんきゅうの傾向けいこう
2. 自分の映画えいがにおけるストーリーの組くみ立たて方かた
3. 人気にんきがある映画えいがの共通点きょうつうてん
4. 映画製作えいがせいさくに対たいする姿勢しせいの変化へんか
questions.translation_en:
At a lecture, a film director is speaking.

M: Since I was a child, I’ve wanted to work in film production, so I studied various ways of developing movie stories and arrived at my current style. When I think about structuring an original film, I develop the story based on three elements. First, I present a problem — something happens that needs to be solved. Then, as the protagonist works to solve the problem, there’s an unexpected development, and in the end, the problem is resolved. Through this process, the protagonist grows. This applies whether it’s a love story or a historical film.

What is the director talking about?
1. Recent trends in film research
2. How he structures stories in his films
3. Common features of popular films
4. Changes in his attitude toward filmmaking.
questions.expl_ko: 정답: 2번 (自分の映画におけるストーリーの組み立て方). 근거: 음성 「ぼくがオリジナルの映画の構成を考えるときは3つの要素で物語を展開させます。まず最初に問題の提示…予想外の展開…問題が解決する」 — 자기 영화의 스토리 구성법. 오답: 1. 최근 연구 동향 아님. 2. 정답. 3. 인기 영화 공통점이 아니라 본인 방식. 4. 자세 변화도 아님. 포인트: 「ぼくが~ときは…要素で展開させます」 본인 방법론 제시.

questions.script_html:
会社かいしゃで社長しゃちょうと女おんなの社員しゃいんが話はなしています。

男おとこ：本田ほんださん。ここ数年すうねん、会社かいしゃの規模きぼが大おおきくなったわけでもないのに電気代でんきだいの支払しはらいが増ふえる一方いっぽうなんですよね。
女おんな：そうですね。これまで照明しょうめいや電気製品でんきせいひんを省しょうエネタイプに替かえてきましたが……。以前いぜん検討けんとうしていた太陽光発電たいようこうはつでんも始はじめてみましょうか。
男おとこ：うーん、その前まえに社員しゃいん全員ぜんいんに無駄むだをもっとなくすことを考かんがえてもらいたいんです。会議室かいぎしつの電気でんきをつけっぱなしにしないとか、1階かいを移動いどうする程度ていどならできるだけ階段かいだんを使つかうとか。あとは、時々ときどき冷房れいぼうの温度設定おんどせっていが低ひくすぎるときがありますよね？ みんなで意識いしきしてやっていかないといけないですよ。
女おんな：そうですね。そのように社内連絡しゃないれんらくで伝つたえます。

社長しゃちょうが言いいたいことは何なんですか。
1. 社員しゃいん1人にん1人にんに電気でんきを節約せつやくしてほしい
2. 電気製品でんきせいひんを省しょうエネのものにしたい
3. 日光にっこうで発電はつでんする機械きかいを使つかいたい
4. 会社かいしゃの設備せつびを長ながく大切たいせつに使つかってほしい
questions.translation_en:
At a company, the president and a female employee are talking.

M: Ms. Honda, in the past few years, even though the size of the company hasn’t really grown, our electricity payments keep increasing.
F: That’s true. Up to now we’ve switched lighting and appliances to energy-saving types… Shall we also start the solar power plan we discussed before?
M: Hmm, before that, I’d like everyone to think more about reducing waste. For example, don’t leave the conference room lights on, and if you’re only moving one floor, try to use the stairs as much as possible. Also, sometimes the air conditioner is set too low, right? We all need to be mindful about these things.
F: I agree. I’ll communicate that internally.

What does the president want to say?
1. He wants each employee to save electricity.
2. He wants to switch appliances to energy-saving ones.
3. He wants to use equipment that generates electricity from sunlight.
4. He wants company equipment to be used carefully for a long time.
questions.expl_ko: 정답: 1번 (社員1人1人に電気を節約してほしい). 근거: 음성 「その前に社員全員に無駄をもっとなくすことを考えてもらいたい…会議室の電気をつけっぱなしにしない…冷房の温度設定…みんなで意識してやっていかないと」 — 사원 한 명 한 명의 절약 의식. 오답: 1. 정답. 2. 절전 가전 교체는 「これまで…替えてきました」 이미 한 일. 3. 태양광 발전은 「その前に」 그 전에 다른 일을 우선. 4. 설비를 오래 쓰자는 얘기 없음. 포인트: 「その前に~してもらいたい」 우선순위 표현.

subsections.title: 問題４
subsections.intro_html: <ruby>問題<rt>もんだい</rt></ruby>4では、<ruby>問題用紙<rt>もんだいようし</rt></ruby>に<ruby>何<rt>なに</rt></ruby>もいんさつされていません。まず<ruby>文<rt>ぶん</rt></ruby>を<ruby>聞<rt>き</rt></ruby>いてください。それから、それに<ruby>対<rt>たい</rt></ruby>する<ruby>返事<rt>へんじ</rt></ruby>を<ruby>聞<rt>き</rt></ruby>いて、1から3の<ruby>中<rt>なか</rt></ruby>から、<ruby>最<rt>もっと</rt></ruby>もよいものを<ruby>一<rt>ひと</rt></ruby>つ<ruby>選<rt>えら</rt></ruby>んでください。

questions.script_html:
女：こう熱帯夜ねったいやが続つづくとエアコンは欠かかせませんよね？
1. エアコンはなくてもいいんですか？
2. え？どうしてエアコンを使つかわないんですか？
3. エアコンつけて寝ねないと寝ねれないですよね
questions.translation_en:
F: When these tropical nights keep continuing, you can’t go without air conditioning, right?
1. Is it okay even without an air conditioner?
2. Huh? Why don’t you use the air conditioner?
3. Yeah, you can’t sleep without turning on the air conditioner, right?
questions.expl_ko: 정답: 3번 (エアコンつけて寝ないと寝れないですよね). 근거: 음성 「こう熱帯夜が続くとエアコンは欠かせませんよね？」 — 에어컨이 필수라는 동의 구함. 오답: 1. 「なくてもいい」는 반대 의미라 부적합. 2. 「使わない」는 화자가 사용 안 한다는 전제, 발화와 어긋남. 3. 정답. 포인트: 「~欠かせませんよね？」=~을 빼놓을 수 없죠? 동의 유도 표현엔 같이 동의하는 응답.

questions.script_html:
女：伊藤さん。2時にじから予定よていしてた打うち合あわせだけど、時間じかんずらしてもらえない？
1. あ、私わたしはいつでも構かまいません
2. 打うち合あわせの時間じかんを長ながくするんですか？
3. 2時にじからで大丈夫だいじょうぶです
questions.translation_en:
F: Ito-san, about the meeting scheduled for two o’clock — could we move the time?
1. Oh, I’m fine anytime.
2. Are we making the meeting longer?
3. Two o’clock is fine.
questions.expl_ko: 정답: 1번 (あ、私はいつでも構いません). 근거: 음성 「2時から予定してた打ち合わせだけど、時間ずらしてもらえない？」 — 시간 변경 요청에 OK 응답. 오답: 1. 정답. 2. 「長くする」는 시간 늘리기로 오해. 3. 「2時からで大丈夫」는 변경 요청과 모순. 포인트: 「~ずらしてもらえない？」=~을 늦춰/옮겨 줄 수 없어? 시간 조정 요청.

questions.script_html:
男：中野さん、最近さいきん卓球部たっきゅうぶの練習れんしゅう休やすみがちだけどどうしたの？
1. 試合しあいが近ちかいから休やすみたくないんだ
2. ごめん、ちょっとバイトが忙いそがしくて
3. 練習れんしゅうがないから一人ひとりでやってたんだ
questions.translation_en:
M: Nakano, you’ve been skipping table tennis practice a lot lately. What’s up?
1. I don’t want to skip since the match is soon.
2. Sorry, I’ve been a bit busy with my part-time job.
3. There wasn’t practice, so I was doing it alone.
questions.expl_ko: 정답: 2번 (ごめん、ちょっとバイトが忙しくて). 근거: 음성 「最近卓球部の練習休みがちだけどどうしたの？」 — 결석 이유 묻는 질문. 오답: 1. 「休みたくない」는 결석하지 않는다는 뜻으로 사실과 어긋남. 2. 정답(이유 + 사과). 3. 「練習がないから」는 부의 사정과 모순. 포인트: 「~がちだ」=자주 ~하다. 부정적 경향에 이유 답변.

questions.script_html:
男：もうすぐ会議かいぎの時間じかんですけど山本やまもと課長かちょう、昼ひるごはん食たべに行いったきりですね。
1. まだ戻もどられてないんですか？
2. 課長かちょう、これから昼食ちゅうしょくですか？
3. あ、もう帰かえってこられたんですか？
questions.translation_en:
M: It’s almost time for the meeting, but Section Chief Yamamoto hasn’t come back since going out for lunch.
1. He hasn’t come back yet?
2. Is the section chief going for lunch now?
3. Oh, has he already returned?
questions.expl_ko: 정답: 1번 (まだ戻られてないんですか？). 근거: 음성 「昼ごはん食べに行ったきりですね」 — 「~たきり」 점심 가서 안 돌아옴. 오답: 1. 정답. 2. 「これから昼食」는 아직 안 갔다는 의미라 모순. 3. 「もう帰ってこられた」는 돌아왔다는 의미로 어긋남. 포인트: 「~たきりだ」=~한 채 그대로다. 그 후 변화 없음.

questions.script_html:
女：店長てんちょう、修理しゅうりを頼たのんでいた冷蔵庫れいぞうこですが、買かい替かえるほかないそうです。
1. あー、直なおせないんですか
2. 直なおせるんですね。よかったです
3. 直なおせるかどうかまだわからないんですね
questions.translation_en:
F: Manager, about the refrigerator we asked to repair — they said there’s no choice but to replace it.
1. Ah, it can’t be fixed?
2. So it can be fixed. That’s good.
3. We still don’t know if it can be fixed, right?
questions.expl_ko: 정답: 1번 (あー、直せないんですか). 근거: 음성 「修理を頼んでいた冷蔵庫ですが、買い替えるほかないそうです」 — 「~ほかない」 다른 방법 없음→수리 불가. 오답: 1. 정답. 2. 「直せるんですね」는 정반대 해석. 3. 「まだわからない」도 보고 내용과 어긋남. 포인트: 「~ほかない」=~할 수밖에 없다. 다른 선택지 부재 표현.

questions.script_html:
女：課長かちょうの送別会そうべつかい、「出席しゅっせき、欠席けっせきに関かんわらず早はやく返事へんじくれ」って小野おのさんが言いってたよ。
1. 出でる人ひとだけ連絡れんらくすればいいんだね
2. 行いけないなら早はやめに返事へんじするんだね
3. 出席しゅっせきできない人ひとは連絡れんらくいらないって思おもってたよ
questions.translation_en:
F: For the section chief’s farewell party, Ono said, ‘Please reply soon whether you’re attending or not.’
1. So only people who can go need to reply.
2. If you can’t go, reply early, right?
3. I thought people who can’t attend don’t need to reply.
questions.expl_ko: 정답: 3번 (出席できない人は連絡いらないって思ってたよ). 근거: 음성 「出席、欠席に関わらず早く返事くれ」 — 출석/결석 상관없이 회신. 오답: 1. 「出る人だけ」는 출석자만이라 「関わらず」와 모순. 2. 「行けないなら」는 결석자만으로 한정 → 마찬가지로 모순. 3. 정답(기존 인식과 다름 → 자연스러운 반응). 포인트: 「~に関わらず」=~에 상관없이. 전체 대상 조건.

questions.script_html:
女：森もりさん。[セミナー]当日のお弁当べんとう、スタッフの分ぶんを含ふくめて30個こ予約よやくをお願いおねがいします。
1. スタッフの分ぶんだけで30個こですね。
2. 予約よやくするお弁当べんとうは全部ぜんぶで30個こですね。
3. スタッフのお弁当べんとうは別べつに注文ちゅうもんするんですね
questions.translation_en:
F: Mori-san, please reserve 30 boxed lunches for the seminar day, including the staff’s portion.
1. So, 30 just for the staff, right?
2. So, a total of 30 boxed lunches to reserve, right?
3. You’re ordering the staff’s lunches separately, right?
questions.expl_ko: 정답: 2번 (予約するお弁当は全部で30個ですね). 근거: 음성 「スタッフの分を含めて30個予約をお願いします」 — 「~を含めて」 스태프 분 포함 총 30개. 오답: 1. 「スタッフの分だけで30個」는 스태프만 30개로 오해. 2. 정답(총 30개 확인). 3. 「別に注文」도 따로 주문이라 「含めて」와 어긋남. 포인트: 「~を含めて」=~을 포함해서. 총합 표현 확인.

questions.script_html:
男：今日のサンプルの[ミーティング]だけど、「部長ぶちょう抜ぬきでやってくれ」って部長ぶちょうから[メール]が来きたよ。
1. じゃ、部長ぶちょうが来きてから始はじめよう
2. 今日、部長ぶちょう来こないんだ
3. あー、今日は[ミーティング]中止ちゅうし
questions.translation_en:
M: About today’s sample meeting — the manager sent an email saying, ‘Go ahead without me.’
1. Okay, let’s start after the manager arrives.
2. So the manager isn’t coming today.
3. Ah, so today’s meeting is canceled.
questions.expl_ko: 정답: 2번 (今日、部長来ないんだ). 근거: 음성 「部長抜きでやってくれって部長からメールが来たよ」 — 「~抜きで」 부장 없이. 오답: 1. 「来てから始めよう」는 참석 전제라 모순. 2. 정답(부장 불참 확인). 3. 「ミーティング中止」는 진행하라는 지시와 어긋남. 포인트: 「~抜きで」=~ 없이/빼고. 인원 제외 표현.

questions.script_html:
女：駅前えきまえのカラオケ、今度こんどの土日どにちに限かぎり半額はんがくって[チラシ]で見みたけど行いかない？
1. 毎週土日まいしゅうどにちは半額はんがくなんだね。行いこうか？
2. 平日へいじつが半額はんがくになるなら平日へいじつだね
3. 今度こんどの週末しゅうまつだね。土曜どようでもいい？
questions.translation_en:
F: I saw a flyer that the karaoke place in front of the station is half price only this weekend. Want to go?
1. Oh, it’s half price every weekend? Shall we go?
2. If it’s half price on weekdays, then weekdays are better.
3. This weekend, huh? Is Saturday okay?
questions.expl_ko: 정답: 3번 (今度の週末だね。土曜でもいい？). 근거: 음성 「今度の土日に限り半額」 — 「~に限り」 이번 토일만 한정. 오답: 1. 「毎週土日」는 매주로 확대 해석. 2. 「平日が半額」는 정반대. 3. 정답(이번 주말 + 일정 제안). 포인트: 「~に限り」=~에 한해. 일회성 한정 표현.

questions.script_html:
男：課長かちょう、みどり社みどりしゃに来年らいねんの[イベント]への協力きょうりょくを依頼いらいしているんですが、返事へんじが曖昧あいまいなんです。
1. 改あらためてお礼れいの[メール]を送おくってください
2. じゃ、私わたしから聞きいてみましょうか
3. 受うけてもらえて安心あんしんしました
questions.translation_en:
M: Section chief, I’ve asked Midori Co. to cooperate for next year’s event, but their response is vague.
1. Please send them a follow-up thank-you email.
2. Then, shall I ask them myself?
3. I’m relieved they accepted.
questions.expl_ko: 정답: 2번 (じゃ、私から聞いてみましょうか). 근거: 음성 「協力を依頼しているんですが、返事が曖昧なんです」 — 답이 애매하다 → 확인 행동 제안 적절. 오답: 1. 「お礼のメール」는 수락 후 행동이라 단계 다름. 2. 정답(상사가 직접 확인 제의). 3. 「受けてもらえて安心」은 결정난 상황 응답으로 어긋남. 포인트: 「曖昧だ」=애매하다. 후속 조치 필요 신호.

questions.script_html:
女：2月にがつにみんなで行いくスキー旅行りょこうの[サイト]見みたけど、来月らいげつになってからでないと申もうし込こみできないって。
1. え？まだ時間じかんあるのにもういっぱいなの？
2. じゃ、今月こんげつ中じゅうに予約よやくしなくちゃいけないんだね
3. そう。じゃ、来月らいげつになったらすぐ予約よやくしよう
questions.translation_en:
F: I checked the website for the ski trip we’re all going on in February, but it says we can’t apply until next month.
1. Huh? It’s still early, but it’s already full?
2. Then we have to reserve it this month, right?
3. I see. Then, let’s make the reservation as soon as next month starts.
questions.expl_ko: 정답: 3번 (そう。じゃ、来月になったらすぐ予約しよう). 근거: 음성 「来月になってからでないと申し込みできない」 — 「~てからでないと…ない」 다음 달부터 가능. 오답: 1. 「もういっぱい」는 만석 의미로 어긋남. 2. 「今月中に予約」는 정반대. 3. 정답(다음 달 즉시 예약). 포인트: 「~てからでないと…できない」=~한 후가 아니면 …할 수 없다. 시점 제한.

subsections.title: 問題５
subsections.intro_html: <ruby>問題<rt>もんだい</rt></ruby>5では、<ruby>長<rt>なが</rt></ruby>めの<ruby>話<rt>はなし</rt></ruby>を<ruby>聞<rt>き</rt></ruby>きます。この<ruby>問題<rt>もんだい</rt></ruby>には<ruby>練習<rt>れんしゅう</rt></ruby>はありません。<ruby>問題用紙<rt>もんだいようし</rt></ruby>にメモをとってもかまいません。

questions.script_html:
会議で上司じょうしと社員しゃいん2人にんが[フードコート]の混雑こんざつについて話はなしています。

男1：うちが運営うんえいしている[南ショッピングセンター]なんですが、週末しゅうまつのランチタイムになると[フードコート]が混雑こんざつして席せきが空あくのを待まってる人ひとがたくさんいるんですよね。何かいい案あんはありませんか？
女：[フードコート]の横よこに[イベントスペース]がありますよね？何も置おいていないし、あそこにも座席ざせきを作つくれたらいいんですが…。
男1：そうなんですが、定期的ていきてきに使用しようする予定よていが入はいっているからちょっと難むずかしいですよね。
男2：食事しょくじが終おわった後あとゆっくり座すわってる方かたも多くて、それが混雑こんざつの一因いちいんになっています。だから食たべ終おわった人ひとに声こえをかけて席せきを空あけてもらうというのはどうですか？
女：客きゃくを追おい出だすようにするというのはちょっと…。
男1：それに客きゃくが多い中、[スタッフ]が声こえをかけて回まわるのは無理むりがありますね。
男2：じゃ、早はやく、例たとえば30分以内ふんいないに席せきを空あけてくれた客きゃくに次回じかい使つかえる割引券わりびきけんを渡わたすのはどうですか？食事しょくじは前払まえばらいだから[レシート]に買かった時間じかんが書かいてありますよね。出でる時とき、[スタッフ]にそれを見みせて券けんを受うけ取とってもらうようにするとか…。
男1：ああ、客きゃくも積極的せっきょくてきに席せきを空あけてくれそうですね。今いまの[スタッフ]の人数にんずうでは対応たいおうが難むずかしそうですが…。
女：やっぱり席せきを増ふやすのが優先ゆうせんだと思おもいます。今いまの広ひろさのままでもう少すこし席せきを追加ついかできるんじゃないでしょうか？
男2：席せきと席せきの間あいだが狭せまくなってしまいますよね？
男1：うーん、そうですね。[スタッフ]を増ふやすことにしてお客きゃくさまに進すすんで席せきを空あけていただけそうな方法ほうほうを試ためしてみましょう。その結果けっかを見みて、席せきを増ふやした方ほうがいいか検討けんとうしましょうか。

混雑こんざつ解消かいしょうのためにまず何をすることにしましたか。
1. [イベントスペース]に座席ざせきを作つくる

questions.translation_en:
In a meeting, a boss and two employees are discussing the crowding in a food court.

M1: At the South Shopping Center we manage, the food court gets really crowded during weekend lunch hours, with many people waiting for seats. Do you have any good ideas?
F: There’s an event space next to the food court, right? It’s empty, so how about adding some seats there?
M1: That’s true, but it’s regularly scheduled for use, so that’s a bit difficult.
M2: Many customers stay seated long after eating, which adds to the congestion. How about asking them to leave after they finish eating?
F: Asking customers to leave sounds a bit harsh…
M1: Also, with so many customers, it would be hard for staff to go around and ask.
M2: Then how about giving customers who leave within 30 minutes a coupon they can use next time? Since meals are prepaid, the receipt shows the time. When they leave, they can show it to staff to receive the coupon.
M1: That might make customers more willing to give up their seats. But with our current staff size, it seems hard to manage.
F: I still think adding more seats should be the priority. Even in the same space, we might be able to fit a few more.
M2: But that would make the space between seats narrower, right?
M1: Hmm, that’s true. Let’s try increasing staff a bit and test ways to encourage customers to leave their seats sooner. Based on that result, we can decide whether to add more seats.

What did they decide to do first to reduce the congestion?
1. Add seats in the event space
2. Ask customers to leave after eating
3. Give coupons to customers who leave early
4. Add more seats inside the food court

questions.translation_en:
At a city health event, a city staff member is speaking.

F1: Thank you for coming to the City Health Event. There are four halls in this building. In Hall 1, we conduct physical fitness measurements. It’s a simple test that anyone can take to find out their fitness age.
In Hall 2, we introduce exercises that are useful for maintaining health — from easy ones you can do at home or work to slightly more difficult ones. Please give them a try.
In Hall 3, we introduce daily meal plans and cooking methods with a focus on a healthy diet. It’s recommended for people whose nutrition tends to be unbalanced.
In Hall 4, doctors will personally answer any health concerns or questions from 1 p.m. to 4 p.m. Please make use of this opportunity.

M: Wow, there’s a lot going on. Maybe I’ll ask about exercises I can do at the office when I’m busy. I haven’t been exercising lately.
F2: Yeah, that sounds good. You don’t have time to go to the gym anyway. It’d be nice to move your body during your commute or work, right?
M: Right. First, I’ll have them measure my fitness level. That’ll motivate me to try harder.
F2: As for me, I think it’s the daily meal plans. I’ve been wanting to review my diet.
M: But didn’t you say you’ve been having trouble sleeping lately? Why not consult the doctor?
F2: Oh, that’s right. I’ll go there first.

1. Hall 1
2. Hall 2
3. Hall 3
4. Hall 4

Question 2: Which hall does the woman say she’ll go to first?
1. Hall 1
2. Hall 2
3. Hall 3
4. Hall 4
questions.expl_ko: 정답: 1번 (第1会場). 근거: 음성 「第1会場では体力測定を実施…ご自分の体力年齢を測定することができます」 — 남자가 「最近運動してない」고 우선 자신의 체력 수준을 알기 위해 측정부터 권유받음. 오답: 1. 정답. 2. 제2회장(체조)은 「会社でもできる運動」 관심이지만 우선 체력 파악이 선행. 3. 제3회장(식생활)은 영양 치우친 사람 대상으로 본인 해당 아님. 4. 제4회장(상담)은 개별 고민 상담용. 포인트: 「~に合わせて」 본인 체력에 맞춘 운동을 위해 먼저 「体力年齢を測定」.
